nice_guideline_used: CG181 / PH46 / NG28 (cardiovascular risk, dyslipidaemia, hypertension, pre‑diabetes) and NG136 (hypertension)

medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 – ACE‑I is first‑line for hypertension

medications.dose: 5 mg oral tablet once daily (titrate to 10 mg if BP target not met)
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive to achieve BP <140/90 mmHg
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 – CCB is recommended add‑on when BP remains uncontrolled on ACE‑I

medications.purpose: Primary prevention of ASCVD (high QRISK likely) and dyslipidaemia
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/PH46 – Statin first‑line when QRISK ≥10 % or metabolic‑syndrome present

medications.dose: 500 mg oral tablet once daily, increase by 500 mg weekly to 500 mg twice daily as tolerated (max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually (or earlier if eGFR falls <30 mL/min/1.73 m²)
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity in pre‑diabetes and aid modest weight loss
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 – Metformin first‑line for impaired glucose tolerance when renal function permits

medications.dose: 0.25 mg sub‑cutaneous weekly, titrate every 4 weeks to 1 mg weekly (up to 2 mg if needed)
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually (or when weight loss goal achieved)
medications.purpose: Weight management in obesity with metabolic syndrome; additional glycaemic benefit
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28/CG181 – GLP‑1 RA recommended for obesity with comorbidities when lifestyle measures insufficient

medications.dose: 200 mg oral tablet once daily (after confirmation of iron‑deficiency)
medications.duration: Until ferritin >200 µg/L and Hb normalised, then reassess (typically 3 months)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG108 – Oral iron for confirmed iron‑deficiency anaemia

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive blood‑pressure lowering effect; may cause symptomatic hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP after initiation and dose titration; advise patient to rise slowly

interactions_checked.interaction: No direct interaction; both are safe together if renal function adequate
No interaction; advise spacing from other oral meds if gastrointestinal irritation

contraindications.reason: Renal function unknown; NICE NG28 contraindicates metformin if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Defer initiation until eGFR confirmed ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²; consider DPP‑4 inhibitor if eGFR <30

contraindications.reason: Contraindicated in patients with personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or MEN2; status unknown
contraindications.alternative: Confirm no history before starting; if present, use alternative weight‑loss therapy (e.g., orlistat)

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum creatinine and potassium not provided – required before initiating or up‑titrating ACE‑I, Metformin, and any future RAAS‑modifying agents (NICE NG136, NG28).
Liver function tests not available – needed before starting atorvastatin (NICE CG181).
Full lipid profile missing – required to confirm dyslipidaemia and monitor response (NICE CG181).
QRISK calculation not available – assumed high given obesity, hypertension, pre‑diabetes (NICE CG181).
Smoking and alcohol use not documented – relevant for cardiovascular risk and medication counselling.
Iron studies (ferritin, transferrin saturation) not available – ferrous sulphate to be started only after confirming iron‑deficiency (NICE NG108).
Allergy status unknown – ensure no known allergy to ACE‑I, statins, GLP‑1 RA, or iron.
Pregnancy status not recorded – ACE‑I, statin and GLP‑1 RA are contraindicated in pregnancy; verify contraception if female of child‑bearing potential.
treatment_summary: The patient with obesity‑related metabolic syndrome and uncontrolled hypertension on lisinopril requires additional antihypertensive therapy (amlodipine) and primary‑prevention lipid lowering (atorvastatin). Metformin and semaglutide are recommended to address pre‑diabetes and obesity, pending confirmation of renal function and exclusion of contraindications. Oral iron is planned once iron‑deficiency is confirmed. All choices follow NICE CG181/PH46/NG28 and NG136 recommendations, with monitoring and safety checks outlined.
